chunks.text: # Attendance Policy
1. A minimum of 75% attendance is mandatory in each course to be eligible to write the end-semester examination.
2. Students with attendance between 65% and 74% may be granted condonation on medical or other genuine grounds, subject to approval by the Head of Department, with a fine of â‚¹500 per course.
3. Students with attendance below 65% are detained and must repeat the course in a subsequent semester.
4. Attendance for medical leave is only condoned if a medical certificate is submitted within 7 days of resuming classes.
5. Attendance shortage appeals must be submitted to the Examination Cell at least 10 days before the start of end-semester examinations.

6. Students on approved official duty (sports, hackathons, technical events representing the college) will have those days marked as "on-duty" and counted as present, provided prior written approval was obtained from the HOD.
# Examination Regulations
1. End-semester examinations are conducted for a maximum of 100 marks per theory course, with a passing threshold of 40%.
2. Internal assessment (mid-term tests, assignments, quizzes) contributes 30% of the total course marks; the end-semester exam contributes the remaining 70%.
3. A student must have at least 75% attendance (or approved condonation) to be issued a hall ticket.
4. Makeup examinations are granted only for students who miss the end-semester exam due to medical emergencies, family emergencies, or approved official duty, supported by valid documentary proof.
5. Requests for makeup examinations must be submitted in writing to the Controller of Examinations within 5 working days of the missed exam, along with supporting documents.
6. Revaluation requests can be submitted within 10 days of result declaration, with a fee of â‚¹300 per course.
7. Malpractice during examinations results in cancellation of that course's exam and may lead to disciplinary action by the Academic Council.
1. Hostel gates close at 21:30 on weekdays and 22:30 on weekends; late entries require prior written permission from the warden.
2. Outstation leave requests must be submitted via the hostel portal at least 24 hours in advance, along with parent/guardian consent.
3. Ragging in any form is strictly prohibited and will result in immediate expulsion from the hostel and disciplinary action as per UGC anti-ragging regulations.
4. Room changes are permitted only at the start of a semester, subject to warden approval and availability.
5. Mess fees are charged quarterly; a rebate is provided for approved leave periods exceeding 5 consecutive days.
6. Visitors are allowed only in the common visiting area during designated hours (16:00-18:00) and must register at the security desk.
1. Each student may borrow a maximum of 4 books at a time for a loan period of 14 days.
2. Overdue books incur a fine of â‚¹2 per day per book.
3. Reference books, journals, and rare collections are for in-library reading only and cannot be borrowed.
4. Lost or damaged books must be replaced or paid for at twice the current market price of the book.
5. The e-book and journal portal is accessible using the student's institutional login credentials from both on-campus and off-campus networks.
6. Silence must be maintained in the reading halls at all times; group discussion rooms are available on the first floor and must be booked in advance.
# Placement Policy
1. Students become eligible for campus placements starting from the 5th semester (3rd year), except for internship drives which may open from the 3rd semester for select companies.
2. Each company sets its own minimum CGPA, branch eligibility, and backlog criteria; these are published on the placement portal at the start of each drive.

3. A student who accepts and confirms an offer from a company is not permitted to sit for further placement drives in the same academic year unless it is a "dream company" as defined by the Placement Cell, in which case a "one dream company" exception applies.
4. Students must complete a mandatory resume review and a mock interview with the Placement Cell before being allowed to register for any core company drive.
5. Attendance at pre-placement talks and eligibility workshops is compulsory for students intending to sit for that company's drive.
6. Placement offers are subject to the company's own background verification and final round outcomes; the college does not guarantee employment.
# Scholarship Criteria
1. The Merit Scholarship requires a CGPA of 8.5 or above with no active backlogs in any semester.
2. The Need-Based Financial Aid requires submission of an income certificate showing family income below â‚¹3,00,000 per year, verified by the Dean of Student Affairs.
3. The Sports Excellence Scholarship requires proof of a state or national level sporting achievement within the current or previous academic year.
4. Scholarship applications are accepted twice a year, at the start of each semester, through the Student Financial Aid portal.
5. Students receiving any scholarship must maintain a minimum of 75% attendance and no failing grades to continue receiving disbursements.
# Grievance Redressal Policy
1. Academic grievances (grading disputes, attendance disputes) should first be raised with the concerned faculty member, then escalated to the Head of Department if unresolved within 7 days.
2. Non-academic grievances (hostel, harassment, ragging, infrastructure) can be submitted anonymously or by name through the Student Grievance Portal.
3. The Grievance Redressal Committee is required to acknowledge a complaint within 48 hours and resolve or respond with a status update within 15 working days.
4. Grievances related to harassment or ragging are handled on priority by the Anti-Ragging and Internal Complaints Committee, with confidentiality maintained throughout.
